Arbelos

GeometryCirclesArea
What it shows: A big half-circle holding two smaller ones, with a knife-shaped gap between them.
How to play: Drag the dot N along the bottom line, or focus it and use the arrow keys. Press a button to jump to another spot.
Look for the math

Move the dot N and the knife changes shape. Yet the number written beside the circle on the upright PN always matches the number for the knife. Why should a circle and a curved gap agree?

The upright at the join

Write AN = a and NB = b. The big semicircle has radius (a + b)/2. A point on a circle is a geometric mean of the two parts of a diameter through it: a short use of similar triangles gives

PN = √(a × b)

That is also the height of the whole chord through N: the full tangent t in the article is 2 × PN. The logic test checks this at a thousand positions of N, and again with the applet's own square-root formula from its bytecode.

Area: the circle matches the knife

The knife is the big half-circle minus the two small ones. Its area is

½π((a+b)/2)² − ½π(a/2)² − ½π(b/2)² = πab/4

The circle drawn on PN has radius PN/2, so its area is πPN²/4 = πab/4 too. This is Archimedes' Proposition 4. The article's problem uses the three complete circles instead of the three half-circles: there the gap is twice as big, and with t = 2PN it becomes S = πt²/8 — the same number for any radii that give the same tangent, as the test confirms.

The boundary arcs

The arc of a semicircle of diameter d is πd/2. So the big arc is π(a+b)/2, which is exactly the left arc πa/2 plus the right arc πb/2. The page calls this obvious, and the test verifies it for every N.

About the original

The Java applet drew a red big semicircle, two grey small ones, a black upright and a draggable blue point at N — the same construction shown here in the site's colours. The cut-the-knot article it came from now carries a GeoGebra figure rather than the Java applet, and the applet's own "about" string was a leftover from a polygon applet; neither changes the mathematics. One tiny applet quirk is not copied: it only accepted a mouse release a couple of pixels above the diameter line, although its point sat on the line. Here you can drop N anywhere along AB.

Press N in the middle, then drag N close to A or B. The knife and its circle change size together, but their two numbers stay equal.
